claim: Lens 440 mm above the mat with a 26 mm-equivalent lens sees a 586 x 439 mm frame
law: Pinhole camera: frame = height x sensor size / focal length, on the 35 mm-equivalent 4:3 frame (34.62 x 25.96 mm)
check: claimed 439 mm (frame depth), estimate 439 mm (frame depth) (ratio 1.00)

claim: The frame stays on the 450 mm deep mat with the phone's placement in the tray allowed for
law: Pinhole camera: frame depth 439 mm at 26 mm; with 3.3 mm of placement stack (S7) the lens must be 25.76 mm equivalent or longer, 1 % under a quoted 26 mm that is itself rounded (independent review 2026-10-25). Lowering the lens to 420 mm gives 15.3 mm a side and fits lenses of 24.2 mm and longer: proposed to Amish as D2, since 440 mm was his decision (N3)
check: 26 mm (35 mm-equivalent focal length) >= 25.76 mm (35 mm-equivalent focal length)

claim: A visible-light camera does not reliably separate opaque HDPE from PP or identify carbon-black plastics; these go to Unsure
law: Polymers are told apart by C-H overtone absorption in the short-wave infrared (Neo et al. 2022, as cited in WasteWise Scan WSC-PRB-001), not by visible colour; carbon black pigment prevents NIR sorting of black packaging (WRAP)
check: The design claims a limit, not a capability: 9 % of items (assumed stream) are routed to Unsure (WML-CAL-001 section 8)
closed_by: WML-CAL-001 section 8; PR-002 not met by design

claim: An 8 h shift of 500 scans (tap-to-scan, screen asleep between scans, voice on, button linked) uses 30 % or less of a 4,000 mAh battery
law: Energy balance: 7.5 J a scan, 0.03 W asleep, 0.5 W for 1 s of voice, 0.005 W Bluetooth link; battery 15.4 Wh

claim: The 10,000 mAh power bank puts about 26.7 Wh into the phone battery
law: Conservation of energy: 37 Wh x 0.85 boost x 0.85 charger

claim: A firm 5 N tap on the screen moves the picture on the mat by less than 1 mm (one grid line's width)
law: Cantilever bending of the 25 x 25 x 2 aluminium post and arm, E = 69 GPa (6063); bolted joints and clamps taken as rigid; the lens's own 0.12 mm drop is left out, which opposes the axis turn, so the figure is conservative
closed_by: WML-CAL-001 section 11; WML-BLD-001 first check 'Stand rigid'

claim: The phone's placement in the tray keeps the picture within the 5.3 mm margin
law: A whole-stand tilt barely moves the picture (0.24 mm a degree: the lens moves one way, the axis turns the other); the phone does: 7.7 mm a degree of axis tilt, 5.1 mm a degree of yaw, plus bump slack in the window. First verdict: Fails, fix proposed (34 mm window and a free phone: 2.0 mm slack plus 0.72 deg yaw, 5.7 mm). Fix F5: 32 mm window (1 mm slack) and the phone pushed against the far lip (no yaw); with 0.3 deg of tray tilt (assumed) the stack is 3.3 mm
closed_by: WML-DEC-001 F5 (fix implemented: tray window, BLD step 7, first check)

claim: In shade on a 40 C Pune afternoon the phone, used tap-to-scan, stays below the 45 C Li-ion charge limit
law: Steady heat balance, h = 10 W/(m2 K) over both faces (0.024 m2); Li-ion charge window 0 to 45 C (Battery University BU-410). In direct sun (about 10 W absorbed) the phone would reach about 85 C, so the rig stands in shade. With the screen on and charging (case B) the phone runs about 10 K over the air, so that fallback holds only below about 35 C (independent review 2026-10-25)
closed_by: WML-CAL-001 section 13; WML-BLD-001 safety stop S4 (shade); PR-020

claim: Loose cells put in the steel hazard box are much less likely to short across their terminals
law: A cell whose terminals touch a conductor (the steel walls, another cell, a can) discharges through it and heats; lithium cells can then go into thermal runaway. Taping terminals is the standard control (UCLA EHS, battery safety)
check: First verdict: Fails, fix proposed (a bare steel box with a sand floor; terminals could touch the walls or each other). Fix F3: the terminals of every loose cell are covered with PVC tape before it goes in, and cells are laid in the 50 mm sand bed clear of the walls; a tape roll lives in the box
closed_by: WML-DEC-001 F3 (fix implemented: BOM line 5, PRC safety, PR-018)

claim: The 50 mm sand bed absorbs the heat of one phone-size cell in thermal runaway with a mean rise under 100 K
law: Heat balance: 15.4 Wh x 8 (assumed upper bound on total heat release against stored electrical energy) into 6.0 kg of sand at 830 J/(kg K): bulk heat capacity only; local temperature near the cell (hundreds of C), venting and spread to other cells are not assessed. The steel box keeps the fire from paper and film; sand does not stop a cell in runaway

claim: The painted hardboard mat stays flat when wet, dirty items lie on it
law: Hardboard takes up water through unsealed faces and edges: 24 h thickness swelling up to 25 % for 3.2 mm board (EN 317 rating, Moelven hardboard datasheet); a coating on one face only also cups the board as the other face swells
check: First verdict: Fails, fix proposed (the build plan painted and varnished the top face only). Fix F2: prime, paint and varnish both faces and all four edges, so the board is sealed all over and the coatings balance. That it then stays flat is not shown: chips and scratches let water in (independent review 2026-10-25); a 24 h wet-cloth soak and cup measurement at TRL 4 confirms it

claim: The model never certifies chemical content, food-contact suitability or hazardous-waste status
law: A photo records reflected visible light; it carries no chemical analysis
check: Scope claim (PRB out of scope; PRC safety)

claim: The user triggers each scan without repeated reaching at shoulder height
law: Two-link arm (Drillis and Contini proportions, Winter 2009) for the 5th percentile Indian woman (stature 1,356 mm, Nag, Nag and Desai 2003); ISO 11226 screens upper arm elevation above 60 deg for static postures (a tap a minute is not static; the 59 deg moves to 51 or 68 deg with the shoulder 100 or 200 mm behind the bench edge)
check: First verdict: Plausible (tapping the screen needs 59 deg upper arm elevation at about one scan a minute, at the 60 deg screen). Fix F1: a Bluetooth shutter button on the bench edge, 45 mm in from the user's edge at bench height, takes the photo; no reach to the phone
closed_by: WML-DEC-001 F1 (fix implemented: BOM line 12, model, BLD, PR-015)

claim: A user at the 5th percentile can read the result (a 40 mm bin number) on the screen lying flat at 1,215 mm
law: Visual angle of the foreshortened symbol: the 5th percentile user's eye is 54 mm above the screen and 415 mm back, 82.6 deg off the screen normal; a 10 mm icon subtends 11 arcmin against the 16 arcmin minimum of ISO 9241-303 (first verdict: Fails, fix proposed). Fix F1: the result fills the screen in the class colour with the bin number at least 40 mm tall, and the phone says the bin number aloud by default. ISO 9241-303 assumes a near-normal view; at 83 deg the digit is squashed about 7.7 to 1 and glare and contrast loss are likely, so legibility is confirmed by a trial with a short user (independent review 2026-10-25); colour and voice do not depend on it

claim: The rig adds little exposure beyond the existing handling of sharps and dirty items, apart from the stored cells of C1 and C2
law: Cut-resistant gloves, no handling of items closer to the camera, hazards to the box (PRC safety)

claim: The 8-bit model file is about 4.4 MB
law: Parameters x 1 byte + 5 % file overhead (MobileNetV3-Large, 5.4 M parameters less the ImageNet classifier plus two heads)

claim: Photo to result in 300 ms or less on a low-cost phone
law: 217 M multiply-accumulates at 1.2 to 4.9 GMAC/s (TensorFlow Models, MobileNet README: 44 ms on a Pixel 1) plus preprocessing
check: 201 ms at the slow end from a preview-size frame (20 ms preprocessing); 331 ms if a full 12 MP frame is decoded first, which the independent review (2026-10-25) put at 100 to 300 ms on an A53-class phone. Met only if the app classifies a preview-size frame; to measure

claim: 400 hazard items with 3 misses or fewer show hazard recall of at least 98 % at 95 % confidence, for the evaluation population
law: One-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bound; valid for an independent sample of the evaluation population only: hazards collected on purpose and photos from one site are not that, so field recall can be lower; report each hazard type separately

claim: About 230 field images per label give 90 % accuracy on answered items at 70 % coverage
law: Power-law learning curve, error = 0.03 + a n^-0.5 anchored at 25 % for 100 images (assumed); power laws fit deep-learning learning curves (Hestness et al. 2017), but the constants for field waste photos are unknown
check: 128 to 591 images per label across the sensitivity cases; the design figure of 300 covers six of the nine cases. The review recalls a scaling exponent nearer 0.3 for ImageNet (Hestness et al. 2017, to check), which would need about 330

claim: About 66 % of items get an answer (63 % graded, 3 % true hazard flags) at 90 % grade accuracy
law: Selective classification: abstaining on the least-confident share u removes 2u of the errors (assumed); stream composition assumed
check: Corrected after the independent review (false hazard alarms leave the graded pool): 66 %, 4 points under PR-004; rests on the assumed stream, enrichment factor and perfect abstention on camera-blind items

claim: About 1,065 answered items estimate a 90 % accuracy to within 2 points (95 %)
law: Normal approximation to the binomial, half-width 1.96 sqrt(p(1-p)/n)

claim: Labeling 10,000 photos takes about 72 h (labeling only; capture and NIR ground truth for camera-blind grades excluded)
law: Photos x 20 s x 1.3 review

claim: A phone image classifier can tell broad material classes apart from one photo
law: TrashNet: six classes of single items photographed with phones on a plain board were told apart (Thung and Yang 2016; the reported accuracy is to recheck against the CS 229 report, independent review 2026-10-25); a clean board is a weak proxy for the field
check: The principle is shown on clean photos; field accuracy by grade is PR-001 and PR-002 (at risk) and M4

claim: At full resolution a molded 6 mm resin code digit spans at least 20 pixels (pixel count only)
law: Pixel pitch on the mat = frame width / 4,000 px; 20 px a character is the design figure (assumed). Legibility of embossed, same-colour codes also depends on lens sharpness and light, not shown here

claim: The model and its activations need about 8 MB of the phone's 3 GB of memory (camera frame buffers, about 48 MB at 12 MP, come on top)
law: Weights plus the two largest activation tensors (112 x 112 x 64, 8-bit, double-buffered)

claim: The shutter button's CR2032 cell lasts at least three months of shifts
law: 225 mAh at 0.05 mA mean while linked (assumed, no datasheet); cheap buttons may draw 0.1 to 0.5 mA, and above about 0.45 mA the cell fails the 78-shift screen (independent review 2026-10-25)
check: 562 shifts at 0.05 mA; 62 at 0.45 mA. The screen tap stays as the fallback; measure the bought button

claim: Option B: the wide camera 450 mm over the tray floor sees the whole 600 x 400 mm tray
law: Frame = 2 h tan(FOV / 2), 102 x 67 deg (Camera Module 3 Wide)

claim: Option B: a 40 mm bottle cap spans at least 16 px at a 1,280 px detector input
law: Pixel pitch = frame width / 1,280 px; small-object detectors need about 16 to 32 px (assumed); an 11 mm button cell is only about 13 px

claim: Option B: a 20,000 mAh power bank runs the Pi 5 and display for an 8 h shift
law: Energy balance: Pi 5 idle 2.7 W, display 1.5 W, detector bursts 6 W for 3 s (assumed); 74 Wh x 0.85 boost

claim: Option B: the detector answers a 1,280 px tray photo in about 1 s on the Pi 5
law: YOLOv8n at 640 px is 8.7 GFLOP (Ultralytics); x4 at 1,280 px; 20 to 40 GFLOP/s effective on the Pi 5 (assumed)

claim: Option B: hazard recall of 98 % holds for items at least half visible in a tray of 10 to 20
law: Detection recall falls for occluded objects; no field data for waste trays
check: Untested; would need its own field evaluation set
